solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticising Belgium needing illumination about origin of long-term urban decay

indicators.note: the criticising word goes round the letter picked out next

parts.note: panning a show or book means criticising it harshly

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
light is illumination

explanation.surface: Someone attacks Belgium for needing more street lighting to stop a slow decline in its towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of long-term' gives L, which 'about' puts inside PANNING. 'long-term' looks like part of the definition, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the decline of a district whose property loses value because redevelopment is proposed but delayed.

clue.text: Nutritional compound for most of soccer team? I will tuck in

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: to tuck in is to be pushed inside something, here the number

parts.note: a soccer side has eleven players, so ten is most of it; the question mark flags the loose idea

explanation.surface: A sports dietician asks what supplement most of the football team should take, and says they'll eat it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck in' reads like eating, but it tells you to put I inside TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins are the nitrogen-containing compounds in meat, eggs and beans that the diet needs for growth.

clue.text: Securing personal best is not yet appreciated

definitions.meaning: getting in front of the time you set before, beating your own record
having ideas too advanced to be accepted by people now

explanation.surface: An athlete sets a new record but nobody notices yet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a visionary whose ideas the present generation is not ready to value.

clue.text: Enthusiastic rising star securing opening in television

indicators.note: the reversed star holds the next letter inside it
in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A keen young star on the way up lands a first break on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nuts about something means being wildly keen on it, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Protective item affording you doze, snooze and kip?

definitions.text: Protective item affording you doze, snooze and kip?

parts.words: Protective item affording you doze, snooze and kip?
parts.note: doze, snooze and kip are all relatives of the word nap, its kin, so the cloth that guards your clothes at table offers you the nap family

explanation.surface: An item that seems to protect you while you take a series of short sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as NAP + KIN: the three sleep words are all kin of NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A table cloth square laid on the lap guards clothing from spilt food, so it is a protective item.

clue.text: A means to support calamity or surprise

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: a blow is a sudden misfortune or calamity
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A device for holding something up in a disaster, or a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bowled over or greatly amazed by something is the informal sense here, a strong synonym of astonish.

clue.text: Always demanding abandonment of banalities

indicators.note: abandonment suggests letters thrown about wildly, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps insisting that trite remarks be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Never satisfied, always wanting more, is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Drama: foolish men involved in unavoidable contradiction

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the three words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A play in which silly men are caught up in an inescapable paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'involved' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a choice between two equally bad options, either of which impales you.

clue.text: Trust the French — writer remaining unknown

parts.note: le is French for the
anon, short for anonymous, signs work whose writer is unknown

explanation.surface: A French author who trusts in staying anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone for support is to rely on them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Work repeatedly round part of hospital without a roof

indicators.note: the two copies go round the hospital department
repeatedly means the work abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: Surgeons operate again and again around a ward that has lost its roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus or car with no roof is described with this hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Keep beginnings of old business and start to rally

indicators.note: the beginnings of two words are their first letters

parts.note: in tennis, a serve starts each rally

explanation.surface: Advice to hang on to a long-standing firm and begin to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or festival is to follow or honour it, a sense shared with obey.

clue.text: Frontless lingerie item creating a stir

indicators.note: without its front means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment combining chemise and panties

explanation.surface: A daring piece of underwear with no front causes a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirl of water or air moving in a circle is a stirring motion in the current.

clue.text: Back lead craftsman — that will involve one not taking sides

indicators.note: the reversed symbol takes the numeral inside it
back means the symbol is reversed

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
I is the Roman numeral one
an artisan is a skilled craftsman

explanation.surface: Support the head craftsman, who will bring in someone neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as head or principal, but it is the metal Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: Supported by both of two parties rather than one is the political sense, so neither faction is favoured.

clue.text: Sweet stuff seeing mega-pulsar spinning

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomer sees sweetness in a giant rotating star.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar boiled from the sap of a Canadian tree is a sweet substance.

clue.text: Definitely not convenient to limit most of enemy's retreat

indicators.note: to limit is to bound, so the nearby word encloses the rest

parts.note: near means conveniently close at hand

indicators.note: retreat means the shortened word goes back, reversed
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: A general sees it handy to curb the retreat of the bulk of the enemy forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal British exclamation used to refuse flatly, much like 'not likely'.

clue.text: Nuisance about airmen needing fine oil

indicators.note: the nuisance word goes about the other pieces

parts.note: a pain is a nuisance
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is made up of airmen
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An annoyance for pilots who need good quality oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuel oil distilled from petroleum and burnt in lamps and heaters, known in the US as kerosene.

clue.text: Turned round holding single from Parisian showing little appreciation of music

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the following pieces
turned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: round means plump, fat
one is a single
de is French, a Parisian's word for from

explanation.surface: Someone spun round clutching a solo record from a Paris singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned round' looks like a single reversal signal, but 'round' is the word reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to tell musical notes apart, hence not appreciating music well.

clue.text: Mob hero is bundle of nerves

parts.note: a gang is a mob
a lion is a celebrated hero, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: A gangland hero who is actually a nervous wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bundle of nerves' suggests a jittery person, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy, a cluster of nerve cells forms a mass outside the brain, literally a bunch of nerve tissue.

clue.text: Stop omitting intro in jazz piece, taking up instrument

indicators.note: the shortened stop sits in the reversed jazz piece
in a down clue taking up means reading upwards, reversed

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime jazz

indicators.note: omitting the intro means the first letter goes

parts.note: to quit is to stop

explanation.surface: A musician quits a jazz number before the intro and switches instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed musical device strummed or plucked, central to rock and folk.

clue.text: Welsh girl cheered last members of rugby teams

parts.note: glad means cheered, pleased

indicators.note: the last members of the two words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A girl from Wales delighted at the end of the rugby matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name of Welsh origin, from Gwladys.

clue.text: Tropical grass, repulsive, trimmed after rising smell

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, reversed
trimmed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: gross means repulsive
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A tropical grass gone disgusting and cut back after a whiff rises from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal grass grown in hot countries for grain and syrup, a crop plant.

clue.text: Put an end to possible cause of alcoholism?

definitions.meaning: to frustrate or stop a rumour or plan
whisky from Scotland, a drink that might lead to alcoholism

explanation.surface: Stopping something that might drive a person to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to quash a rumour and Scotch whisky, a spirit drunk to excess by some.

clue.text: Urging son to participate in playing tennis to break ice

indicators.note: the jumbled group breaks the frozen word apart, sitting inside it
to participate in is to take part inside, so the letter goes into the jumble
playing suggests letters in play, moved around

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent pushes their son to play tennis to ease awkwardness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to participate in' puts S into the anagram of the racket sport, giving NSISTEN, before 'to break' splits ICE. 'break ice' reads as the idiom for easing tension, which hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent demand, urging, pressing someone hard, is the sense of the noun.

clue.text: Make unclear comments about book, forgetting book at the end

indicators.note: forgetting means the letter is left out
says which letter goes, the final one

parts.note: a blurb is the publisher's praise printed on a book's cover

explanation.surface: A reviewer whose remarks on a novel lose the thread at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear or smudge an image so it cannot be seen sharply.

clue.text: Upset for bar bouncer, say

definitions.note: a bouncer is a big lie, so one who tells one is an example

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, reversed

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A doorman tips over a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but in Chambers a bouncer is also a whopping lie, so its teller fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells a bouncer, a whopping untruth, is a fibber, so this is an example.

clue.text: Feeling strangely warm beside fireplace

parts.note: at means beside, as in at the door
an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Someone sits next to the hearth and feels oddly hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tingling all over, as with excitement, is a feeling of strange warmth.

clue.text: Significant card — hearts — securing current victory

indicators.note: the card holds the current symbol inside it

parts.note: a trump card outranks the other suits
I is the symbol for electric current
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A bridge player wins with a heart as the trump suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A great success or win, a synonym for conquest.

clue.text: (ORIGINAL CLUE) Legislator to look different about following honest source of money or (REVISED CLUE) Legislator to look different about following male criminal

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: the word for different goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: other means different

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawmaker seems unusual when tracking down a man who broke the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed version has two clues: the original appears to give one R too many, so the revised version is annotated.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the House of Lords help make British law, so a lord is a lawmaker.
